e.etymology: A respelling of Evelyn that brings out Eva and the -lynn ending. Evelyn began as an English surname drawn from the Norman woman's name Aveline.
Best known as the elf princess of Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings, where it means noble maiden in his Elvish language. Arwen is also a Welsh name, from ar-, an intensifier, and gwen, blessed or fair.
namesakes: Arwen (elf princess played by Liv Tyler in The Lord of the Rings films)

assoc.t: Arwen, the elf princess in The Lord of the Rings

e.etymology: A pet form of Matilda, from the Germanic elements maht, might, and hild, battle. It was common in the 1890s and is returning with Millie and Hattie.
A modern American coinage that sets the -lin ending on Day-, in the pattern of Jaylin and Kaylin. It is given to both girls and boys.
From Arabic Isa, the name of Jesus in the Quran, widely used in the Middle East and across Muslim Africa. The writer and actress Issa Rae made the name familiar for girls in the US.
namesakes: Issa Rae (creator and star of HBO's Insecure)

assoc.t: Issa Rae, creator and star of Insecure
issa, meme slang for it's a, as in issa vibe

e.etymology: A French pet form of Anne, from Hebrew Hannah, grace or favor. Its US peak around 1960 coincided with the fame of the Mouseketeer Annette Funicello.
From a surname with two sources: the Irish name Colmán, little dove, borne by many early saints, and an English occupational name for a charcoal burner.

assoc.t: Coleman, maker of camping stoves, lanterns and coolers

e.etymology: A spelling of Kinsley, an English surname from a Yorkshire village, the woodland clearing of a man called Cyne, an Old English name from the word for royal.
A Spanish pet form of María, perhaps modeled on Italian Mariella. María is the Spanish form of Mary, from Hebrew Miriam.
A modern American name in the family of Aaliyah, Alayah and Alaia, with no meaning of its own.
An Arabic name, especially common in Lebanon, usually explained as serious or earnest; some link it to generosity instead.
namesakes: Jad Abumrad (creator and longtime host of Radiolab)

e.etymology: A modern name with no single source: in the US a spelling in the family of Kyra, Keira and Kiara, and also used in India. Kaira is separately an Estonian name related to Kairi.
A short form of Italian Margherita and Spanish Margarita, from Greek margarites, pearl. Saint Rita of Cascia, canonized in 1900, spread it. Rita is separately an Indian name from Sanskrit.
namesakes: Rita Moreno (EGOT-winning actress in West Side Story)

assoc.t: Lovely Rita, the Beatles song about a meter maid
Hurricane Rita, which hit the Gulf Coast in 2005
Rita's Italian Ice, a frozen-dessert chain

e.etymology: A respelling of King, the English royal title, from Old English cyning. King itself became a common American first name in the 2010s.

assoc.t: sounds the same as the word king

e.etymology: A recent American coinage that adds the -ly ending of Everly and Finley to Wren, the small songbird.
A later Hebrew short form of Yehoshua (Joshua), common among Jews of the Second Temple period. It is the form behind Greek Iesous and so the original of the name Jesus.

assoc.t: Yeshua, the Hebrew name of Jesus of Nazareth

e.note: Widely understood as the original Hebrew name of Jesus, so it carries strong religious weight.

e.etymology: From the English word maven, an expert or connoisseur, borrowed from Yiddish meyvn, from Hebrew mevin, one who understands. It rose as a name in the 2010s, close in sound to Haven and Maeve.

assoc.t: maven, an everyday word for an expert

e.etymology: A spelling of Carmela, the Italian and Spanish name honoring Our Lady of Mount Carmel. Carmel is Hebrew for garden or orchard. Italian immigrants brought it to the US around 1900.

assoc.t: sounds like Carmela Soprano of The Sopranos

e.meaning: hill of Wine, an Old English name meaning friend
e.etymology: An English surname from a place in Buckinghamshire, in Old English Wine's hlaw, the mound or hill of a man named Wine, friend. Long a boys' name, it is now given mostly to girls.

assoc.t: Winslow, Arizona, from the Eagles' Take It Easy
the Winslows, the family in the sitcom Family Matters

e.etymology: The English word for the shaft shot from a bow, from Old English arwe. It came into use as a first name in the 2010s alongside Archer.

assoc.t: arrow, the everyday word for what a bow shoots
Arrow, the CW series about DC's Green Arrow

e.etymology: A spelling of Jasmine, from the fragrant flower, whose name goes back through French and Arabic to Persian yasaman. Jasmin is the usual form in Germany and Finland and a men's name in Bosnia.

assoc.t: Princess Jasmine in Disney's Aladdin
jasmine, the fragrant flower, tea and rice

e.etymology: A modern spelling of Hayden, an English surname from place names built on Old English heg, hay, with denu, valley, or dun, hill.
The English word honesty, from Old French honeste and Latin honestas, used as a virtue name in the style of Faith, Grace and Charity.

assoc.t: Billy Joel's 1978 ballad Honesty
honesty, a garden plant with silvery seed pods

e.meaning: form of Rosaline, tied to Latin rosa, rose
e.etymology: A variant of Rosaline shaped by the Scottish place name Roslin or Rosslyn. Rosaline goes back to Rosalind, a Germanic name later read as Spanish rosa linda, pretty rose.

assoc.t: Roslyn, village on Long Island, New York
Roslyn, Washington, where Northern Exposure was filmed

e.etymology: From Arabic farah, joy or happiness. It is common across the Muslim world; the spelling Farrah became familiar in the US through actress Farrah Fawcett.

assoc.t: sounds like Farrah, as in actress Farrah Fawcett

e.etymology: From Greek ekho, sound. In Greek myth Echo was a mountain nymph cursed to repeat only the last words spoken to her; she pined for Narcissus until only her voice was left.

assoc.t: Amazon Echo smart speaker
Marvel's Echo, a deaf Native American hero
Echo chainsaws and leaf blowers

e.note: An everyday word and the name of Amazon's smart speaker; expect repeat-after-me jokes.

e.etymology: A modern American coinage that joins the word name Ember to the -lee ending, on the pattern of Kimberly and Everly. Emberly is the more common spelling.
A modern respelling of London, the English capital, influenced by Lynn. The city name goes back to Roman Londinium; its earlier meaning is unknown.

assoc.t: London, capital of the United Kingdom

e.etymology: A respelling of Colt, the English word for a young male horse, which is also a surname and a short form of Colton.

assoc.t: sounds like Colt, the American gun maker
sounds like the Indianapolis Colts football team

e.etymology: From Althaia, a queen in Greek mythology, a name linked to Greek althos, healing. Richard Lovelace's 1642 poem To Althea, from Prison brought it into English use.
namesakes: Althea Gibson (first Black tennis player to win a Grand Slam title)

assoc.t: Althea, a Grateful Dead song
althea, a common name for the rose of Sharon shrub

e.etymology: From the Slavic name for the morning star, the planet Venus as seen at dawn, built on the word for day. In Slavic folklore Danica personifies that star.

assoc.t: Danica Patrick, the race car driver

e.etymology: Usually described as Irish and often glossed as chief, though no Gaelic source for it has been confirmed.
